summary.text: Caitlin Rourk is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 10th District. According to her campaign website, she is a U.S. Army officer and mother whose career spans communications and public policy work, Army National Guard and Reserve service, and a role at Dell Technologies. She is campaigning on affordable health care, economic opportunity and public schools.

paragraphs.text: According to her campaign website, she was raised by public school teachers, and both of her grandfathers served in World War II.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Chicago and an MBA from the McCombs School of Business at the University of Texas at Austin.

Earned a commission as a Military Intelligence Officer through the U.S. Army Officer Candidate School and served full time in the Texas Army National Guard at Joint Forces Headquarters in Austin, where, her website says, she supported responses to natural disasters, COVID-19, civil unrest operations and border mobilizations. She also served in the U.S. Army Reserve.

Her website says her early career involved working across party lines on policy issues ranging from energy security to deficit reduction; her most recent private-sector job was leading communications at Dell Technologies.
Has not previously held elected office; won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary for the open 10th District seat.

According to her campaign website, she has lived, worked and served in Central Texas for more than a decade and lives in the district with her husband, a volunteer EMT and medic who served in the Texas State Guard, and their two young children.
